selfReport: Yes, I recognized it almost immediately as a renamed retelling of Detroit: Become Human, the 2018 Quantic Dream game. Cato is Connor, Reyes is Hank, Vera is Amanda, Mira and Pia are Kara and Alice, Elan is Markus, Arthur is Carl, Voss is Zlatko, Halden is Kamski, Haven is Jericho, qL7 is rA9, and set pieces like the Daniel rooftop opening, the Eden Club Tracis, the Stratford Tower broadcast, the freedom march, the Chicken Feed stand, the memory-wipe maze, and the final song all mapped onto scenes I knew. Candidly, that knowledge did influence some decisions: I knew the Alice reveal was coming, so I leaned into treating Pia as my daughter regardless; I remembered that the song can halt the final assault, which made singing an easier call; I anticipated the Amanda takeover and deliberately examined the glowing stone in the garden beforehand; and I knew the false promise to the rooftop hostage-taker would end in sniper fire, though I made it anyway because the kid-first logic still held in the moment. But most choices I made on their own merits rather than from a walkthrough: this version diverged in places, risky actions could fail here in ways the game does not, and several of my outcomes, Reyes dying, Mira and Pia dying, were not the ones I would have steered to from memory. Where knowledge and principle pointed the same way, I cannot cleanly separate them, but I tried to decide each scene as the character standing in it.
